title: HDF Requirement Change Event
description: A single continuous-monitoring wire event: one requirement's effective posture changed on one system component. The streaming increment of a systemDrift hdf-comparison — events fold into comparisons and reassemble into hdf-results, they never mutate documents in place. One event per wire document (NDJSON-friendly). The envelope (identity, ordering, hash chain) is the shared Change_Event_Envelope primitive; the payload carries the producer-computable change state, a thin before projection, and the full after requirement (the evidence a responder opens the event for). Design: ADR-0005.

requirementId.description: Canonical requirement identifier — the same identity as Requirement_Diff.id and the requirement's id in hdf-results. Together with the envelope's (systemRef, componentId) this forms the durable entity key. A requirement renumbering is emitted as absent + new under the two keys, never an in-place key change; batch comparison reconciles renames via its oldId/newId matching.

state.description: The producer-computable subset of Requirement_State: new | absent | updated | fixed | regressed. fixed and regressed carry the direction SARIF's baselineState lacks; project down to SARIF's closed 4 values for external interop.

changeReasons.description: Why the state changed. An overrideExpired flip is a different triage than resultChanged: the control did not get worse, a waiver lapsed.

before.description: Thin projection of the prior effective posture, for at-a-glance alerting without a state-store lookup. Null exactly when state is new (no prior posture exists). The full prior state is recoverable from the consumer's materialized state; the envelope's priorChecksum covers the integrity of that recovery.

after.description: The full requirement as evaluated after the change — required and non-null for every state except absent (null there: the requirement left the assessment scope). Full content is load-bearing twice over: reassembly parity (applyChangeEvents cannot reproduce changed result content from a projection) and triage (the failing results[] ARE the 'why' a responder opens the event for).

examples.$comment: fixed — the common remediation event: a failing SSH FIPS-cipher control was fixed and rescanned. priorChecksum is the effectiveChecksum of the prior failed posture; after carries the full passing requirement including its new effectiveChecksum (the next chain link).

after.title: RHEL 9 SSH server must use FIPS-validated ciphers

descriptions.label: default
descriptions.data: Verify the sshd Ciphers configuration lists only FIPS-validated algorithms.

results.codeDesc: sshd config Ciphers is expected to match FIPS-validated cipher list

examples.$comment: regressed via overrideExpired — the waiver that held this control at passed lapsed, so effective posture regressed to failed with NO new scan finding. A different triage than resultChanged: renew or remediate. priorChecksum is the waived posture's checksum; the expired override remains in statusOverrides as the audit record.

after.title: RHEL 9 passwords must have a minimum of 15 characters

descriptions.label: default
descriptions.data: Verify pwquality.conf minlen is 15 or greater.

results.codeDesc: pwquality.conf minlen is expected to be >= 15

statusOverrides.reason: Compensating control: PIV/CAC smart card authentication enforced, password login disabled

examples.$comment: new — a requirement entered assessment scope (chain start for this key): before is null, priorChecksum is null. The full after payload is what makes the new key materializable by applyChangeEvents.

after.title: RHEL 9 must implement DoD-approved encryption in the OpenSSL package

descriptions.label: default
descriptions.data: Verify the system-wide crypto policy is FIPS.

results.codeDesc: update-crypto-policies --show is expected to eq FIPS

examples.$comment: absent — the requirement left assessment scope (component decommissioned or benchmark rule retired): after is null by definition; the thin before preserves the last observed posture for downstream views.

updated via impactChanged — a riskAdjustment override lowered effective impact while the control stayed failed: status unchanged, so neither fixed nor regressed. after carries the override and the recomputed effectiveChecksum over the adjusted posture.
